scope: Aggregation-side specification: measure-level stars -> domain stars, Part C summary, Part D summary, overall rating, icons.

source.document: Medicare 2026 Part C & D Star Ratings Technical Notes
source.extraction: pdftotext -layout (poppler 24.02.0); all numeric strings cross-verified against pdfplumber extraction of the same PDF
source.page_citation_convention: Printed page numbers as shown in the PDF footers ('(Last Updated ...) Page N'), not physical PDF page indices.
source.precision_law: All numbers in this file are decimal strings copied verbatim from the PDF; no float round-trips.

summary_rating_rule.method: Weighted mean of measure-level stars (not of domain stars). Part C summary uses Part C measure stars; Part D summary uses Part D measure stars.
summary_rating_rule.formula: summary = sum_i(weight_i * star_i) / sum_i(weight_i), over the contract's rated measures for the relevant Part; measures without a rating are excluded from both sums.
summary_rating_rule.verbatim_weighting: The summary and overall ratings are calculated as weighted averages of the measure stars. For the 2026 Star Ratings, CMS assigns the highest weight to the improvement measures, followed by outcome and intermediate outcome measures, then by patient experience/complaints and access measures, and finally process measures. New measures included in the Star Ratings are given a weight of 1 for their first year of inclusion in the ratings; in subsequent years the weight associated with the measure weighting category is used. The weights assigned to each measure and their weighting category are shown in Attachment G.
summary_rating_rule.verbatim_computation: In calculating the summary and overall ratings, a measure given a weight of 3 counts three times as much as a measure given a weight of 1. For any given contract, any measure without a rating is not included in the calculation. The first step in the calculation is to multiply each measure’s weight by the measure’s rating and sum these results. The second step is to divide this sum by the sum of the weights of the contract’s rated measures. For the summary and overall ratings, half stars are assigned to allow for more variation across contracts.
summary_rating_rule.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 11, “Summary and Overall Ratings: Weighting of Measures”
summary_rating_rule.weights_table_reference: Attachment G, Tables G-1 (Part C) and G-2 (Part D), pp. 117-118 — reproduced in measure_weights_2026 below.

org_type_applicability.MA-PD: Receives Part C summary, Part D summary, and overall rating. Highest rating = overall rating.
org_type_applicability.MA-only: Receives Part C summary only (includes 1876 Cost and PFFS without drug benefits, MSA). Highest rating = Part C summary rating.
org_type_applicability.PDP: Receives Part D summary only. Highest rating = Part D summary rating.
org_type_applicability.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 4, “Table 3: Relation of Organization Types to Contract Types and Highest Rating”

minimum_rated_measures.verbatim: To receive a Part C and/or Part D summary rating, a contract must meet the minimum number of rated measures. The Parts C and D improvement measures are not included in the count of the minimum number of rated measures. The minimum number of rated measures required is determined as follows: If the total number of measures required for the organization type is odd, divide the number by two and round it to a whole number. If the total number of measures required for the organization type is even, divide the number of measures by two.
minimum_rated_measures.note: The Parts C and D improvement measures are not included in the count of the minimum number of rated measures.
table_6_footnotes: * Note: Does not apply to MA-Only, 1876 Cost, and PFFS contracts which do not offer drug benefits.
† Note: 1876 Cost contracts which do not submit data for the MPF measure must have ratings in 5 out of 9 measures to receive a Part D rating.
minimum_rated_measures.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 12, “Methodology for Calculating Part C and Part D Summary Ratings, Table 6”

adjustments_order.verbatim: There are two adjustments made to the results of the summary and overall calculations described above. First, to reward consistently high performance, CMS utilizes both the mean and the variance of the measure stars to differentiate contracts for the summary and overall ratings. If a contract has both high and stable relative performance, a reward factor is added to the contract’s ratings. Details about the reward factor can be found in the section entitled “Applying the Reward Factor.” Second, the summary and overall ratings include a Categorical Adjustment Index (CAI) factor, which is added to or subtracted from a contract’s summary and overall ratings. Details about the CAI can be found in the section entitled “Categorical Adjustment Index (CAI).” The summary and overall rating calculations are run twice, once including the improvement measures and once without including the improvement measures. Based on a comparison of the results of these two calculations a decision is made as to whether the improvement measures are to be included in calculating a contract’s final summary and overall ratings. Details about the application of the improvement measures can be found in the section entitled “Applying the Improvement Measure(s).” Lastly, standard rounding rules are applied to convert the results of the final summary and overall ratings calculations into the publicly reported Star Ratings. Details about the rounding rules are presented in the section “Rounding Rules for Summary and Overall Ratings.”
order: 1. Compute raw weighted mean of measure stars (with >= 6 decimal digits of precision), twice: with and without the improvement measure(s).
2. Add reward factor (r-Factor) where earned; computed both with and without improvement measures (see reward_factor).
3. Add or subtract CAI; applied both with and without improvement measures (see cai).
4. Choose with- vs without-improvement result per the hold-harmless rules (see improvement_hold_harmless).
5. Round the final value to the nearest half star per Table 22 (see rounding). Rounding happens LAST; no half-star rounding occurs mid-pipeline.
adjustments_order.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 13, “Completing the Summary and Overall Rating Calculations”

rounding.verbatim: The results of the summary and overall calculations are rounded to the nearest half star (i.e., 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0).
rounding.tie_convention_verbatim: For example, a summary or overall rating of 3.749999 rounds down to a rating of 3.5, and a rating of 3.750000 rounds up to rating of 4. That is, a score would need to be at least halfway between 3.5 and 4 (having a minimum value of 3.750000) in order to obtain the higher rating of 4.
rounding.tie_convention: Band lower bounds are inclusive: a raw value exactly at X.X50000/X.750000/X.250000 boundary belongs to the HIGHER half-star band (e.g., exactly 3.750000 -> 4.0; 3.749999 -> 3.5).
rounding.clamps: Displayed scale is 0 to 5.0; Table 22 maps raw [0.000000, 5.000000] onto {0, 0.5, ..., 5.0}. Raw values cannot exceed 5 (measure stars are 1-5; reward factor and CAI additions are applied to the raw score before rounding, and the top band '4.750000 to 5.000000 -> 5.0' is the published cap).
rounding.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 23, “Rounding Rules for Summary and Overall Ratings, Table 22”

improvement_hold_harmless.preamble_verbatim: Since high performing contracts have less room for improvement and consequently may have lower ratings on these measure(s), CMS has developed the following rules to not penalize contracts receiving 4 or more stars for their highest rating.
ma_pd_steps_verbatim: There are separate Part C and Part D improvement measures (C30 & D04) for MA-PD contracts. a. C30 is used in calculating the Part C summary rating of an MA-PD contract. b. D04 is used in calculating the Part D summary rating for an MA-PD contract. c. Both improvement measures will be used when calculating the overall rating in step 3.
Calculate the overall rating for MA-PD contracts without including either improvement measure.
Calculate the overall rating for MA-PD contracts with both improvement measures included.

If an MA-PD contract in step 2 has 4 or more stars, compare the two overall ratings. If the rating in step 3 is less than the value in step 2, use the overall rating from step 2; otherwise use the result from step 3.
For all other MA-PD contracts, use the overall rating from step 3.
ma_only_steps_verbatim: Only the Part C improvement measure (C30) is used for MA-Only contracts.
Calculate the Part C summary rating for MA-Only contracts without including the improvement measure.
Calculate the Part C summary rating for MA-Only contracts with the Part C improvement measure.

If an MA-Only contract in step 2 has 4 or more stars, compare the two Part C summary ratings. If the rating in step 3 is less than the value in step 2, use the Part C summary rating from step 2; otherwise use the result from step 3.
For all other MA-Only contracts, use the Part C summary rating from step 3.
pdp_steps_verbatim: Only the Part D improvement measure (D04) is used for PDP contracts.
Calculate the Part D summary rating for PDP contracts without including the improvement measure.
Calculate the Part D summary rating for PDP contracts with the Part D improvement measure.

If a PDP contract in step 2 has 4 or more stars, compare the two Part D summary ratings. If the rating in step 3 is less than the value in step 2, use the Part D summary rating from step 2; otherwise use the result from step 3.
For all other PDP contracts, use the Part D summary rating from step 3.
improvement_hold_harmless.highest_rating_rule: The hold harmless applies to the contract's HIGHEST rating: overall for MA-PD, Part C summary for MA-Only, Part D summary for PDP (Table 3). For an MA-PD, the Part C and Part D SUMMARY ratings always include the respective improvement measure (steps 1a/1b); only the overall rating is computed with/without.
improvement_hold_harmless.condition: The 'has 4 or more stars' condition is evaluated on the step-2 (without-improvement) rating; contracts below 4 stars always use the with-improvement result (step 3).
improvement_hold_harmless.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 13-14, “Applying the Improvement Measure(s)”

improvement_measure_rating_minimums.eligibility_verbatim: Further, to receive a Star Rating in the improvement measures, a contract must have measure scores for both years in at least half of the required measures used to calculate the Part C improvement or Part D improvement measures. Improvement scores are not calculated for reconfigured regional contracts until data is available for the reconfigured structure from both years. Improvement scores are not calculated for consolidated contracts in their first year.
improvement_measure_rating_minimums.footnote: * Note: Does not apply to MA-Only, 1876 Cost, and PFFS contracts which do not offer drug benefits.
improvement_measure_rating_minimums.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 6, “Improvement Measures, Table 4”
improvement_measure_rating_minimums.extraction_note: Identical to 2025 Table 4: the three new 2026 measures (C04, C05, C13) are excluded from the improvement attainment-measure set (significant specification change / new), leaving the same denominators.

cai.applied_to: Overall rating, Part C summary rating, Part D summary rating (separate CAI value per rating type; MA-PD Part D and PDP Part D have distinct tables).
cai.verbatim: The Categorical Adjustment Index (CAI) is an analytical adjustment factor that is added to or subtracted from a contract’s Overall and/or Summary Star Ratings to adjust for the average within-contract disparity in performance for Low Income Subsidy/Dual Eligible (LIS/DE) beneficiaries and disabled beneficiaries. The CAI value (factor) depends on the contract’s percentage of beneficiaries with LIS/DE and the contract’s percentage of beneficiaries with disabled status. These adjustments are performed both with and without the improvement measures included.
cai.derivation_verbatim: The CAI values use data collected for the 2025 Star Ratings. ... Adjusted measure scores are then converted to measure stars using the 2025 rating year measure cutoffs and used to calculate Adjusted Overall and Summary Star Ratings. ... The CAI values are the mean differences between the Adjusted Overall or Summary Star Rating and the corresponding Unadjusted Star Rating for contracts within each final adjustment group. ... Categories were chosen to enforce monotonicity.

initial_groups.interval_convention: Each row is [lower, upper): lower bound inclusive, upper bound exclusive, except the highest group where the upper limit (100.000000) is inclusive; the L10 LIS/DE group is exactly 100.000000.
initial_groups.pdp_grouping: 2026: PDP initial groups use QUARTILES for both LIS/DE and disability (Tables 19-20), as in 2025.

cai.per_contract_source: Per-contract final adjustment categories are published in '2026 Star Ratings Data Table - CAI (Oct 8 2025).csv' (columns: Contract Number, Organization Marketing Name, Contract Name, Parent Organization, Puerto Rico Only, Part C FAC, Part D MA-PD FAC, Part D PDP FAC, Overall FAC); map FAC -> CAI value via Tables 12/15/18/21. Contract LIS/DE and disability percentages themselves are not published.
cai.puerto_rico: Contracts solely serving Puerto Rico get a modified LIS/DE percentage (PR beneficiaries are not LIS-eligible) before categorization; methodology in Attachment O. The published CAI data table flags 'Puerto Rico Only' contracts.
cai.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 16-22, “Categorical Adjustment Index (CAI), Tables 10-21”

reward_factor.eligibility: Computed for every summary/overall rating of every rated contract; a contract earns r-Factor > 0 only if its mean and variance fall in the qualifying cells below. Calculations are performed both with and without the improvement measures included, AND both with and without the new measures (2026 Tables 8-9 carry the 'New Measures' With/Without dimension; new 2026 measures are C04 Improving or Maintaining Physical Health, C05 Improving or Maintaining Mental Health (respecified HOS), and C13 Kidney Health Evaluation for Patients with Diabetes (HEDIS)).
reward_factor.mean_verbatim: The mean is equal to the summary or overall rating before the reward factor is applied, which is calculated as described in the section entitled “Weighting of Measures.”
reward_factor.mean_note: The 'mean' is the raw weighted mean per Weighting of Measures — i.e., BEFORE the reward factor and before CAI.
weighted_variance_steps_verbatim: Subtract the summary or overall star from each performance measure’s star; square the results; and multiply each squared result by the corresponding individual performance measure weight.
Set n equal to the number of individual performance measures available for the given contract.
Set W equal to the sum of the weights assigned to the n individual performance measures available for the given contract.
The weighted variance for the given contract is calculated as: n * SUMWX / (W * (n-1)).
reward_factor.weighted_variance_formula: s_j^2 = n_j / ((n_j - 1) * sum_i(w_ij)) * sum_i(w_ij * (x_ij - xbar_j)^2)  [Attachment H]
reward_factor.variance_categories_verbatim: Categorize the variance into three categories: low (0 to less than 30th percentile), medium (greater than or equal to 30th to less than 70th percentile) and high (greater than or equal to 70th percentile)

r_factor_map.condition: low variance & high mean (mean greater than or equal to 85th percentile)
medium variance & high mean (mean greater than or equal to 85th percentile)
low variance & relatively high mean (mean greater than or equal to 65th & less than 85th percentile)
medium variance & relatively high mean (mean greater than or equal to 65th & less than 85th percentile)

reward_factor.thresholds_note: Final threshold values are PUBLISHED in Tables 8-9. NOTE: the 60% disaster exclusion from reward-factor threshold determination was REMOVED for 2026: 'Removed the 60 percent rule for non-CAHPS measures such that the numeric score values for affected contracts with 60 percent or more of their enrollees in Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) designated Individual Assistance areas at the time of an extreme and uncontrollable circumstance are no longer excluded from the clustering algorithm or from the reward factor calculations.' (Differences, p. 1, item e)
reward_factor.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 14-16, “Applying the Reward Factor, Tables 8-9”; Attachment H, p. 119
reward_factor.formula_extraction_note: GARBLED IN 2026 PDF: the inline variance formula (p. 15) and the Attachment H / Attachment I formulas are set in a math font without a ToUnicode map; pdftotext AND pdfplumber both extract glyph garbage (e.g. '!"#"$%&'(")"*'"#"*!+,--!.'). The formula is recovered from the 2025 Technical Notes (identical wording): n * SUMWX / (W * (n-1)). No NUMERIC values are affected — all digits in Tables 8-9 extract cleanly and were cross-verified with pdfplumber.

overall_rating_rule.method_verbatim: The overall rating for a MA-PD contract is calculated using a weighted average of the Part C and Part D measure stars. The weights assigned to each measure are shown in Attachment G.
overall_rating_rule.rule: The overall rating is the weighted mean over ALL rated Part C + Part D MEASURE stars (one pooled weighted average) — it is NOT a mean of the Part C and Part D summary ratings.
overall_rating_rule.requires_both_summaries_verbatim: For MA-PDs to receive an overall rating, the contract must have stars assigned to both the Part C and Part D summary ratings. If an MA-PD contract has only one of the two required summary ratings, the overall rating will show as “Not enough data available.”
overall_rating_rule.duplicated_measures: Complaints about the Health/Drug Plan (CTM) and Members Choosing to Leave the Plan (MCLP) appear in both Part C and Part D; only ONE instance of each is used in the overall rating.
overall_rating_rule.measure_counts_verbatim: There are a total of 45 measures (33 in Part C, 12 in Part D) in the 2026 Star Ratings. ... These measures share the same data source, so CMS includes only one instance of each of these two measures in the calculation of the overall rating. In addition, the Part C and D improvement measures are not included in the count for the minimum number of measures. Therefore, a total of 41 distinct measures plus the two improvement measures are used in the calculation of the overall rating.
table_7_footnotes: * Note: Does not apply to MA-Only, 1876 Cost, and PFFS contracts which do not offer drug benefits.
† Note: 1876 Cost contracts which do not submit data for the MPF measure must have ratings in 16 out of 32 measures to receive an overall rating.
overall_rating_rule.org_type_applicability: Overall rating exists only for MA-PD contracts (incl. 1876 Cost / PFFS offering drugs). MSA and PDP: N/A. MA-Only: N/A (highest rating is the Part C summary).
overall_rating_rule.rounding: Same Table 22 half-star rounding as the summary ratings, applied after reward factor + CAI + improvement hold-harmless selection.
overall_rating_rule.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 12-13, “Methodology for Calculating the Overall MA-PD Rating, Table 7”

integer_domain_rule.verbatim: A domain rating is the average, unweighted mean, of the domain’s measure stars. To receive a domain rating, a contract must meet or exceed the minimum number of rated measures required for the domain.
integer_domain_rule.rounding_verbatim: The domain ratings are the unweighted average of the star measures and are rounded to the nearest integer.
integer_domain_rule.rounding_note: Rounded to the nearest integer; the Technical Notes state no explicit tie rule for domain ratings, but the document-wide 'traditional rounding rules' (5 rounds up) govern all rounding (see precision_rule).
integer_domain_rule.minimum_measures_rule_verbatim: If the total number of measures that comprise the domain for a contract type is odd, divide the number of measures in the domain by two and round the quotient to the next whole number. If the total number of measures that comprise the domain for a contract type is even, divide the number of measures in the domain by two and add one to the quotient.
table_5_footnotes: * Note: Does not apply to MA-Only, 1876 Cost, and PFFS contracts which do not offer drug benefits.

† Note: 1876 Cost contracts that offer drug benefits and which do not submit data for the MPF measure must have a rating in 3 out of 5 Drug Safety and Accuracy of Drug Pricing (DD4) measures to receive a rating in that domain.
integer_domain_rule.domains_do_not_feed_overall: CONFIRMED: summary and overall ratings are weighted means of MEASURE stars directly; domain stars are display-only and are not an input to any summary/overall calculation.
framework_verbatim: Summary: Part C measures are grouped to calculate a Part C Rating; Part D measures are grouped to calculate a Part D Rating. Summary ratings are calculated from the weighted average Star Ratings of the included measures.
Overall: For MA-PDs, all unique Part C and Part D measures are grouped to create an overall rating. The overall rating is calculated from the weighted average Star Ratings of the included measures.
integer_domain_rule.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 10-11, “Methodology for Calculating Stars at the Domain Level, Table 5”; rounding sentence from Calculation Precision, p. 22

precision_rule.verbatim: The improvement measures, summary, and overall ratings are calculated with at least six digits of precision after the decimal whenever the data allow it. The HEDIS measure scores have two digits of precision after the decimal. All other measures have at least six digits of precision when used in the improvement calculation.
precision_rule.sas_verbatim: CMS and its contractors have always used software called SAS (an integrated system of software products provided by SAS Institute Inc.) to perform the calculations used in producing the Star Ratings. For all measures, except the improvement measures, the precision used in scoring the measure is indicated next to the label “Data Display” within the detailed description of each measure.
precision_rule.no_replication_verbatim: It is not possible to replicate CMS’s calculations exactly due to factors including, but not limited to: using published measure data from sources other than CMS’s Star Rating program which use different rounding rules, and exclusion of some contracts’ ratings from publicly-posted data (e.g., terminated contracts).
where_rounding_occurs: Measure SCORES: rounded to the 'Data Display' precision with traditional (5-up) rounding BEFORE cut point analysis (measure-star assignment).
Measure STARS: integers 1-5; no further rounding.
Improvement measure scores, summary and overall ratings: carried at >= 6 decimal digits; NOT rounded mid-pipeline.
Domain ratings: unweighted mean of measure stars, rounded to nearest integer (display only).
Summary/overall: single terminal rounding to nearest half star per Table 22 after all adjustments.
precision_rule.measure_score_rounding_verbatim: Measure scores are rounded to the precision indicated next to the label “Data Display” within the detailed description of each measure. Measure scores are rounded using traditional rounding rules. These are standard “round to nearest” rules prior to cut point analysis. ... For example, a measure listed with a Data Display of “Percentage with no decimal point” that has a value of 83.499999 rounds down to 83, while a value of 83.500000 rounds up to 84.
precision_rule.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 22, “Calculation Precision”; Rounding Rules for Measure Scores, p. 23

disaster_provisions.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, pp. 7-9, “Data Handling of Measures for Contracts Affected by a Major Disaster”
disaster_provisions.thresholds: SINGLE threshold for 2026: 'The disaster policy specifies a threshold of “25% or more” of the contract's membership at the time of the disaster resided in a FEMA-designated Individual Assistance area.' The 60% rule was removed (Differences, p. 1, item e).
disaster_provisions.new_measure_hold_harmless_overall_verbat: Contracts with 25% or more affected members have a hold harmless provision applied which compares the result of a contract’s overall rating “with” and “without” including all of the applicable new measure(s) and/or respecified measure(s). If the “with” result is lower than the “without” result, then we use the “without” result as the final highest level rating. For the 2026 Star Ratings, two new measures are HOS measures and one is a HEDIS measure. As noted above, HOS measures are adjusted for disasters occurring in 2023 whereas HEDIS measures are adjusted for disasters occurring in 2024. Therefore, the hold harmless provision is conditionally applied for a given contract according to the new measures’ available data. Contracts with data for both the new HEDIS measure and at least one of the new HOS measures are eligible for the new measure hold harmless provision if the percentage of beneficiaries affected by a disaster is at least 25 percent in either 2023 or 2024. Contracts with only available data for the new HEDIS measure are eligible for the new measure hold harmless provision if the percentage of beneficiaries affected by a disaster is at least 25 percent in 2024. Contracts with only data for one or both of the new HOS measures are eligible for the new measure hold harmless provision if the percentage of beneficiaries affected by a disaster is at least 25 percent in 2023.
disaster_provisions.new_measure_hold_harmless_summary_verbat: A similar hold harmless provision is applied for the Part C and D summary ratings, when applicable. If a contract has 25% or more affected members, the Part C and D summary ratings are calculated “with” and “without” including all of the applicable new measure(s) and/or respecified measure(s), and if the “with” result is lower than the “without” result, then we use the “without” result for the final summary ratings. For the 2026 Star Ratings, all new measures are Part C measures with differing disaster year adjustments, and a similar conditional hold harmless provision as described above for the overall rating is applied based on new measures’ available data.
disaster_provisions.best_of_measure_stars: Contracts with 25%+ affected members receive the higher of the 2025 or 2026 measure stars (and corresponding scores) for CAHPS, HOS/HEDIS-HOS, HEDIS, and all other measures (Call Center: no adjustment). If equal, the most recent year's star and score are used.
disaster_provisions.improvement_interaction_verbatim: For affected contracts that reverted back to the data underlying the previous year’s Star Rating for a particular measure for either 2025 or 2026 Star Ratings, that measure is excluded from both the count of measures (used to determine whether the contract has at least half of the measures needed to calculate the relevant improvement measure) and the improvement measures’ calculation. Affected contracts do not have the option of reverting to the prior year’s improvement rating.
sixty_percent_rules: REMOVED for 2026. Verbatim (Differences, p. 1, item e): 'Removed the 60 percent rule for non-CAHPS measures such that the numeric score values for affected contracts with 60 percent or more of their enrollees in Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) designated Individual Assistance areas at the time of an extreme and uncontrollable circumstance are no longer excluded from the clustering algorithm or from the reward factor calculations.' The 2026 disaster section accordingly contains no Reward Factor or Cut Points exclusion bullets.

high_performing_icon.verbatim: A contract may receive a high performing icon as a result of its performance on the Parts C and/or D measures. The high performing icon is assigned to an MA-Only contract for achieving a 5-star Part C summary rating, a PDP contract for a 5-star Part D summary rating, and an MA-PD contract for a 5-star overall rating.
high_performing_icon.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 23-24, “Methodology for Calculating the High Performing Icon”

low_performing_icon.verbatim: A contract can receive a low performing icon as a result of its performance on the Part C and/or Part D summary ratings. The low performing icon is calculated by evaluating the Part C and Part D summary ratings for the current year and the past two years (i.e., the 2024, 2025, and 2026 Star Ratings). If the contract had any combination of Part C and/or Part D summary ratings of 2.5 or lower in all three years of data, it is marked with a low performing icon (LPI). A contract must have a rating in either Part C and/or Part D for all three years to be considered for this icon.
low_performing_icon.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 24, “Methodology for Calculating the Low Performing Icon”

consolidations.verbatim: In the first year following a consolidation, the measure values used in calculating the Star Ratings of the surviving contract will be based on the enrollment-weighted mean of all contracts in the consolidation (see Attachment B).
consolidations.cite: 2026 Star Ratings Technical Notes, p. 24-25, “Mergers, Novations, and Consolidations”

special_rules.displayed_vs_computed: No adjustment alters the displayed overall relative to the computed one beyond the pipeline above; icons are separate flags. Improvement measure NUMERIC scores are not published (only their stars): “The numeric results of these calculations are not publicly posted; only the measure ratings are reported publicly.” (Improvement Measures, p. 5)
